en: Martin Hale lived on a street in northwest Rivermere so quiet it seemed deliberate.
The house was small. The lawn was cut with geometric precision. There were no decorations on the porch. An ageing grey Subaru sat in the driveway.
Nora rang the bell at 10:04 a.m.
He was in his sixties, taller than she had expected, with completely white hair. Navy sweater. Old jeans.
"A reporter calls about a twenty-eight-year-old missing-person case, I check the reporter."
There were no police souvenirs in the living room.

No medals. No framed uniform photographs. No retirement plaque. Only books, plants, an old dog asleep beside a heating vent, and a stack of paper on the dining table aligned with suspicious precision.
He set a mug in front of her and sat opposite.
"I filled out her Missing Person Intake."
"I wouldn't call it that. Second year on the job. I did what I was told."
"Adult missing person. No obvious sign of immediate danger. Travel plans. Train tickets. Statements that she wanted to leave the city."
"Was she ever confirmed on the train?"
"Does that sound like a normal adult voluntarily disappearing?"
Martin lifted his mug but did not drink.
"Because that same week there was a murder the entire city was watching."
"Warehouse fire. Her ex-boyfriend, Evan Cole, was eventually convicted of murder."
"Or police didn't ask the right people."
For the first time, Nora saw irritation in his face.
"Are you here to interview me or accuse me?"
"Then don't line them up before you know what they mean."
They held each other's gaze for a moment.

"Fine. Fact one: my mother disappeared on the night of November nineteenth. Fact two: she'd bought two train tickets for Edmonton the next morning, one for me. Fact three: she didn't take that train. Fact four: on November twentieth, her name appears on a legal document marked received in person. Fact five: that document involved Halden, where Lena Zhou worked."
Martin's eyes moved slowly to the tabletop.
Nora slid the photograph toward him.
He studied it for a long time.
"The warehouse that burned at Alder Yard was Warehouse 4."
"You said you only handled the missing-person intake."
"I was also sent to the fire scene for perimeter control."
"So back then you had two cases. My mother missing. Lena murdered. And you never thought they might be connected?"
"Because on the timeline, they didn't appear to intersect."
Nora followed his eyes to a narrow wooden cabinet against the wall.
"Thinking certain pieces of paper are only personal work notes."
A row of black hardbound notebooks stood inside, arranged by year.
A single white label was fixed to the cover.
He turned several pages and stopped.
A line in faded blue ink read:
Nora looked at the two case numbers.
"I remember these as happening days apart."
He tapped the dates with one finger.
"According to my notebook, they were four hours apart."
zh: Martin Hale住在里弗米尔西北边一条安静得过分的街上。房子不大，草坪修得极整齐，门廊上没有装饰，车道停着一辆灰色老式Subaru。诺拉按门铃的时候，上午十点零四分。
男人六十多岁，比她想象中高，头发已经全白，穿深蓝毛衣和旧牛仔裤。
“记者打电话说要谈二十八年前的失踪案，我当然会查记者。”
客厅没有任何警察纪念品。
没有奖章，没有制服照片，没有退休牌匾。只有书、植物、一只睡在暖气旁边的老狗，以及餐桌上一摞整理得异常整齐的纸。
他把咖啡放在她面前，坐到对面。
“因为我当年填过她的Missing Person Intake。”
“谈不上。我入职第二年。谁让做什么就做什么。”
“成年失踪者，不存在明显危险迹象。有旅行计划，有车票，有人说她想离开城市。”
“这在你看来像一个正常离开的成年人？”
“因为同一周发生了一宗全城都在盯着的谋杀案。”
“仓库火灾。前男友Evan Cole后来被判谋杀。”
第一次，诺拉从他脸上看见一点不悦。
“好。事实一：我母亲十九号晚上失踪。事实二：她买了二十号早晨两张去埃德蒙顿的车票，其中一张给我。事实三：她没有坐那班车。事实四：二十号，她的名字出现在一份亲自签收的法律文件上。事实五：那份文件涉及Halden，而Lena Zhou当时就在Halden工作。”
“Alder Yard的火灾仓库，就是4号仓库。”
“你刚才说你只是做失踪登记。”
“我也被调去火灾现场维持外围。”
“所以当年两个案子，一个是我母亲失踪，一个是Lena被杀，你从来没有想过可能有关？”
“因为时间线上，它们看起来没有交点。”
诺拉顺着他的视线看过去。
“以为某些纸只是自己的工作笔记。”
他打开木柜最下面一层。
里面是一排黑色硬皮笔记本。
封面上只有一个白色标签。
下面隔了三页，又出现另一个编号。
“这两件事我记得隔了好几天。”
“但我的笔记里，它们只隔了四个小时。”
